CFD Analysis: 100mm L2 Rocket Fin Tab — Roll Authority & First-Flight PID Tuning

Date: August 9, 2026
Rocket: "100 mm All Fiberglass Steerable" (OpenRocket model)
Geometry source: 100 mm Rocket Airfoil.step (Fusion 360, one of 4 fins)
Solver: OpenFOAM v2412, simpleFoam (steady incompressible RANS, k-ω SST), Docker local

1. Objective

Characterize the roll torque produced by the trailing-edge control tab of the 100 mm L2 rocket fin across tab deflections of −20° to +20° and three flight velocities (40, 80, 120 m/s), then derive roll-rate PID gains for the first flight. The flight envelope covers both motor options: AeroTech J435WS (Vmax ≈ 91 m/s) and J570W (Vmax ≈ 119 m/s). First flight uses roll control only (rate-null mode, the same controller structure flown on the 67 mm testbed).

2.1 Fin & Tab

Tab span24.0 mm (X = 54.7 → 78.7 mm from root plane)

Root plane → axis distance Daxis44 mm assumed (mid boat-tail; sensitivity in §9)

The STEP assembly contains the fin blade, the control tab (round-nose flap on a spanwise torque rod at Z=61.6 mm from the aft edge), and the internal servo/linkage hardware (excluded from CFD). Internal channels that open into the flow (rod bore at the tip, two chordwise lightening holes, three skin screw pilots) were capped in CAD before meshing.

2.2 CFD frame & deflection convention

AxisMeaning
Xspanwise, 0 at the fin root plane, tip at +110 mm
Ythickness/lateral
Zstreamwise, flow +Z, LE at Z=10 mm, TE at Z=160 mm

δ > 0 moves the tab TE toward +Y. Roll moment about the body axis (parallel to Z at X = −Daxis): M_roll = Mz(origin) + Fy × D_axis. With this convention positive δ produces negative M_roll; only the magnitude matters for tuning — the physical rotation direction is verified on the bench (§7.5).

Figure 1: CFD geometry at −20°, 0°, +20° tab deflection. Green: fin (fincan patch). Red: tab (finTab patch). Bottom row: airfoil sections through the tab span.

6. Roll Plant Model

6.1 Roll inertia (component build-up)

GroupI_roll (10⁻³ kg·m²)
Airframe (tubes, nose, couplers, recovery, motor)10.65
Fin set ×4 (CAD volume integral, D_axis 44 mm)7.65
Total I_roll18.30

Propellant burn changes I_roll by <1% (on-axis mass), so launch and burnout values are treated as equal. The 67 mm testbed was 2.0×10⁻³ — this rocket has 9.2× the roll inertia.

6.2 Plant gain

Rate-loop plant (all 4 tabs driven together): ω̇ [deg/s²] = K_plant(V) · δ [tab deg], with K_plant(V) = 4·Kt(V)/I_roll · 180/π. Weak aero roll damping (strip theory: pole at 0.9–2.7 rad/s over 40–120 m/s) is negligible at the 2 Hz crossover.

7. PID Tuning for First Flight

7.1 Controller structure (as flown on the 67 mm)

Rate-null PID at ~1 kHz: error = 0 − ω [deg/s], output = physical tab degrees (1:1 linkage), clamped ±20°. All four tabs receive the same roll command. Velocity gain schedule scale = min((V_ref/max(|V|,V_min))², 3) with V_ref = 50, V_min = 25 m/s from EKF speed. Integral separation freezes the accumulator while |error| > 40 deg/s. Angle-hold cascade stays off for the first flight.

7.2 Design method

The rate loop through the tab is an integrator: L(s) = Kp·K_plant/s. Following the 67 mm methodology: crossover fc = 2.0 Hz (ωc = 12.6 rad/s), so Kp = ω_c / K_plant(V_ref). Phase margin budget at ωc: servo lag (τ = 32.5 ms) −22.2°, loop delay −0.7°, integral zero (0.6 rad/s) −2.7° → PM ≈ 64° (target ≥ 50°). Kd is unnecessary at this margin and is left 0 (matches all flown configs).

7.3 Recommended gains

ParameterValueNotes
KP0.224tab-deg per deg/s, quoted at V_ref = 50 m/s
KI0.134integral zero at 0.6 rad/s; trims fin misalignment in ~2 s
KD0.0PM already 64°; servo lag limits D usefulness
D_FILTER_CUTOFF_HZ10unchanged (inactive with KD=0)
INTEGRAL_SEP_THRESHOLD_DPS40unchanged
GAIN_SCHEDULE_V_REF / V_MIN / cap50 / 25 / 3unchanged
MIN_CMD / MAX_CMD±20°CFD linear range confirmed to ±20°

For comparison, the 67 mm flew KP = 0.12 / KI = 0.01 at the same V_ref: the 100 mm needs ≈2× the proportional gain because inertia grew 9.2× while total tab torque grew only ~2.9× at matched speed. A conservative fallback (KI = 0.02) gives slower trim of the ~2 deg/s residual from expected fin misalignment but is otherwise equivalent.

Figure 7: velocity profiles (1-DOF with real thrust curves), gain-schedule factor, and effective Kp for both motors. The scale rides the 3× cap below 29 m/s — i.e. briefly off the rod and again late in coast.

7.4 Closed-loop verification

Figure 8: 1 kHz closed-loop simulation with servo lag (32 ms, 923 deg/s slew), ±20° clamp, gain schedule, integral separation, a 120 deg/s launch kick at t = 0.5 s and a constant 0.46° effective tab misalignment (the 67 mm measured −0.46°). The kick is nulled in well under a second on both motors and the misalignment trims to zero without saturating.

7.5 First-flight checklist

  1. Sign check on the bench: with the established spin test, confirm positive roll rate produces the tab direction that opposes it; flip FIN_ROLL_REVERSE_MASK if not. (CFD gives magnitude; mounting orientation sets the sign.)
  2. Rate-null mode only (USE_ANGLE_CONTROL = false); angle cascade (KP_ANGLE = 2.0, cap 60 deg/s) can fly later once rate control is proven.
  3. Expected behavior: control authority is weak below ~30 m/s (schedule capped), strong through boost; expect <12° tab for a 120 deg/s disturbance at V ≥ 50 m/s.
  4. Servo direction/trim per the standard preflight; per-servo biases as calibrated.

// tinkerrocket-idf/projects/flight_computer/main/config.h (100mm L2 rocket)
static constexpr float KP = 0.224f;   // tab-deg per deg/s at V_ref=50
static constexpr float KI = 0.134f;   // integral zero 0.6 rad/s
static constexpr float KD = 0.0f;
// unchanged: MIN_CMD/MAX_CMD ±20, D_FILTER_CUTOFF_HZ 10,
// INTEGRAL_SEP_THRESHOLD_DPS 40, GAIN_SCHEDULE_V_REF 50, V_MIN 25, cap 3.0

# tinkerrocket-sim rocket definition (100mm L2)
rd.dry_mass          = 6.57 + 0.55        # airframe + burned-out motor (J570W)
rd.I_roll_launch     = 1.8298e-02
rd.I_roll_burnout    = 1.8298e-02
rd.fin_tabs.n_tabs   = 4
rd.fin_tabs.V_ref    = 95.0
rd.fin_tabs.Kt_ref   = 1.618e-02   # N·m/deg per tab at 95 m/s (sign per firmware_roll_sign)
rd.fin_tabs.deflection_min = -20.0
rd.fin_tabs.deflection_max = 20.0
rd.roll_damping_K    = 4.13e-04    # N·m/(m/s · rad/s), strip theory

9. Limitations & Uncertainty

SourceEffect on Kt
D_axis assumption 44 mm (boat-tail range 37.5–51.1) -5.9% / +6.4% at the extremes
0.5 mm hinge gaps sealed by mesh resolutionslight overestimate (a few %; leakage ignored)
Flat wall instead of curved boat-tail at rootsmall; tab is mid-span, away from the root
Single fin (no fin–fin interference, no body vortices)consistent with 67 mm methodology
Steady RANS, fully turbulentno dynamic hinge effects; Re high enough
I_roll component model±10% (D_axis and mass-model spread)

Net: treat K_plant as ±15%. The design has PM ≈ 64° and a 2 Hz crossover — a ±15% plant-gain error moves the crossover ±15% and PM by ~±3°, well inside margins. The integral separation and ±20° clamp bound the failure modes; the gains are safe to fly.

10. Reproducing This Analysis

100mm-L2-Rocket-Fin-Tab-Analysis/
    100 mm Rocket Airfoil.step   # source CAD (Fusion 360 export)
    build_geometry.py            # STEP -> 11 deflected STLs (cadquery)
    case_template/               # OpenFOAM case (blockMesh+snappy+simpleFoam)
    run_sweep.sh                 # 33 cases, Docker opencfd/openfoam-default:2412
    postprocess_sweep.py         # force extraction, Kt fits
    roll_inertia.py              # I_roll + damping from .ork + CAD
    generate_report.py           # this report
    results/                     # force/moment histories + logs
    geometry/                    # STLs + previews

python3 build_geometry.py
bash run_sweep.sh                # ~4.5 h on M-series 10-core, 2 concurrent
python3 postprocess_sweep.py
python3 roll_inertia.py
python3 generate_report.py

11. Conclusions

  1. Tab roll authority is highly linear to ±20° at all speeds (R² ≥ 0.9951); Kt per tab = 2.76 / 11.48 / 26.16 mN·m/deg at 40/80/120 m/s.
  2. V² scaling holds within 5.5% across the envelope — Mach ≤ 0.35 keeps the incompressible solver valid.
  3. Roll plant: I_roll = 18.3×10⁻³ kg·m², K_plant(50) = 56 deg/s² per tab-deg.
  4. First-flight gains: KP = 0.224, KI = 0.134, KD = 0 (2.0 Hz crossover, PM ≈ 64°), existing schedule/anti-windup settings unchanged.
  5. Closed-loop sim nulls a 120 deg/s kick in <1 s with <12° tab on both motors.
